correctness.rationale: Kondō’s established Picard lattice NS(S)=U and invariant fibre and section give an integral splitting H²(S,Z)=U⊕T. The primitive 66-eigenvalue on the holomorphic 2-form forces char(g*|T)=Φ66 of degree 20. Since Φ66(1)=1, 1−g* is an integral automorphism of T. Wang and Künneth compute every torsion-free integral cohomology group and π1=Z²; invariant Hodge classes yield H²(O)=0, so the exponential sequence and H³(Z)=Z⁴ imply Br=0. Canonical torsion in Pic⁰ follows from torsion-free H². The exact checker verifies the cyclotomic and rank computations, not an infinite substitute proof.

value.rationale: The motivating quotient realizes canonical index 66, a natural sharp dimension-three extremal example. Its full integral cohomology and vanishing Brauer group are intrinsic torsion-sensitive invariants, unlike rational Betti numbers; Br(S) itself is a divisible rank-20 group, whereas Br(V)=0, and the canonical line bundle retains order 66 in Pic⁰ with zero integral c1. This distinguishes it sharply from classical K-trivial quotient threefolds with nonzero Brauer and provides a natural arithmetic-topological invariant relevant to derived and Brauer comparisons, without claiming downstream theorems.
